FOUNDING_HYPOTHESIS.VERDICT: SIGN-REVERSAL COMPONENT NOT SUPPORTED: 0 of 35 flip-eligible BEARING memories show both a positive and a negative dU task; the Wilson upper bound is 0.09890099232440402. This BOUNDS the rate; it is not merely an absence of observations.
FOUNDING_HYPOTHESIS._kill_criterion: NOT triggered: it required the phenomenon to be absent. What is absent is the sign-reversal COMPONENT; the memory-utility effect itself is large and significant.
FOUNDING_HYPOTHESIS._scope: NOT evidence that harm does not occur in agent memory: one corpus, one reader, one representation, pairs selected to bear. The defensible statement is 'unsupported here', not 'absent'. No harmful-memory RATE is claimed from any stratum -- the pairing is ours in all three, so none yields a natural base rate.

ROBUST_NAIVE_GAP_STATUS._why: F_exec[delta] == 0 for a deterministic reader, so section 4's magnitude clause |mean dU| > F is vacuous and robust == naive by construction. A gap of 0.0 here would imply a measurement was taken; it cannot be taken at this replicate count.

STOPPING_RULE._rule: docs/CONTRAST_FRAMING.md / K report section 16: if BEARING's both-arms-fail is not MATERIALLY below RANDOM's, the instrument cannot detect anything and THAT is the headline. Committed before results existed so it cannot be softened after seeing them.

_reference_floor_policy: prereg section 2 fixes the reference floor as F_exec per BENCHMARK, pooled across tasks. It is computed once here and applied to every stratum's labels. Per-stratum floors are diagnostics only.
_what: K3 per-stratum analysis of the screened main run

cell_concentration._why_reported: the shared task grid is the identifiability fix AND the source of the concentration; they are one design tension. This is why every contrast carries a task-clustered CI and a leave-one-task-out jackknife.

BEARING_vs_MATCHED_CONTROL._clustering_note: cells are NOT independent: the shared grid gives some tasks up to 40 cells. The permutation p is cell-level; the task_clustered_ci and the leave-one-task-out range are what govern whether ONE question drives the difference.
BEARING_vs_MATCHED_CONTROL._null: stratum label shuffled WITHIN memory, so memory identity is held fixed and only the bearing label moves

PAIRED_POWER_STATUS._reading: the effect was DETECTED (CI excludes zero), so no power caveat applies
PAIRED_POWER_STATUS._rule: docs/ZERO_CONTRIBUTORS.md: below ~8 non-zero contributors, declare UNDERPOWERED rather than report a null -- a null at n_effective=5 is a different claim from a null at n=40. The count alone is not sufficient: power depends on the observed spread too, so both are checked.
PAIRED_POWER_STATUS._scope: this flag qualifies a NULL only. A CI that excludes zero means the effect WAS detected, and post-hoc power for a detected effect is a fallacy -- 'could we have found it?' is answered by 'we did'.

BEARING_vs_MATCHED_CONTROL._conditional_caveat: conditions on a non-zero outcome, so it is DESCRIPTIVE and can never be the population claim. The significance verdict comes from the all-memories test below.
BEARING_vs_MATCHED_CONTROL._denominator_note: 60 memories (35 non-zero). Never quote the nominal count alone.
BEARING_vs_MATCHED_CONTROL._governing: the episode-clustered interval governs when it and the memory-level interval disagree
BEARING_vs_MATCHED_CONTROL._why_this_is_the_strongest_form: all 60 memories appear in both strata, so MEMORY IDENTITY CANCELS: 'bearing memories are just better memories' cannot explain a within-memory difference. Task identity does NOT cancel (strata are disjoint in tasks), which is why the quantity is dU and why the task-clustered intervals in perm_contrast remain required.
